newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI credit to industry up in Sept.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI credit to industry up in Sept.

text.p: The State Bank of India (SBI)'s loans to industry grew by 8.45 billion rupees in September, reversing a recent trend of a slowdown in credit growth, its chairman said on Monday.
"Credit grew by about 8.45 billion rupees last month," SBI chairman Pandurang Kakodkar told Reuters.
The recent negative trend in credit growth has been reversed, he said.
Indian banks have been complaining about a slowdown in loans to industry this year. SBI is India's largest commercial bank and its list of clients includes leading blue-chip firms.
Most other banks however said they are yet to see any signs of a revival in credit offtake by the industry.

Last week, SBI reduced its prime lending rate by one percentage point to 14.5 percent in response to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) initiatives to boost liquidity and prompt interest cuts in its monetary policy released on October 19.
